findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; logic is misleading
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` returns false on both branches, so the `FlagSqlExpressions` toggle has no effect. The negated flag check stored in a variable named `enabled` reads as a mistake. A later maintainer could "fix" the inversion and re-enable a path whose backend is now a stub. Make it an explicit unconditional `return false` (or drop the case) and add a comment explaining it is deliberately disabled for CVE-2024-9264.

findings.title: Error message is misleading
findings.body: When SQL expressions are requested, users get the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature exists but was deliberately disabled for security reasons, so the message is confusing. A clearer message such as "SQL expressions are disabled" would help users and support.

findings.title: Other SQL command construction paths still reachable; existing tests likely broken
findings.body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (the legacy rawNode path) is not gated by the feature check. It is now harmless only because `TablesList` returns an error. Existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` (e.g. parser tests that expect table lists) and the SQL command tests probably fail now. They should be removed or updated, and a test added asserting that SQL expressions are rejected.
